questions.stem: SIMLIPAL National Park and Tiger Reserve is located in:
questions.explanation: Simlipal — Mayurbhanj district, Odisha. Tiger reserve, UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Famous for tigers, elephants, Mugger crocodiles, gaurs. Also has Joranda and Barehipani waterfalls.

questions.stem: Match the NATIONAL PARK / RESERVE with its state. A. Periyar.  B. Sariska.  C. Bandhavgarh.  D. Nagarhole. List-II: 1. Kerala.  2. Rajasthan.  3. Madhya Pradesh.  4. Karnataka.
questions.explanation: Periyar — Kerala, tigers, elephants; famous boat safari. Sariska — Rajasthan, Alwar district, tiger reserve. Bandhavgarh — MP, tiger density famously high. Nagarhole / Rajiv Gandhi NP — Karnataka, part of Nilgiri Biosphere.

questions.stem: The world's LARGEST MANGROVE forest, Sundarbans, is famous for:
questions.explanation: Sundarbans (WB + Bangladesh) — Royal Bengal Tigers adapted to mangrove, saline water; famous as swimming tigers. Also estuarine crocodiles, Gangetic dolphins, spotted deer. UNESCO WHS 1987.

questions.stem: KEOLADEO NATIONAL PARK (Bharatpur), Rajasthan, is most famous for:
questions.explanation: Keoladeo / Bharatpur Bird Sanctuary — wetland ecosystem, UNESCO WHS 1985, Ramsar site. Key wintering ground for migratory water-birds including painted storks, herons, pelicans. Siberian cranes used to winter here but have not been sighted since 2002.

questions.stem: ONE-HORNED RHINOCEROS's second-largest population in India (after Kaziranga) is found at:
questions.explanation: Manas National Park (Assam, also a Project Tiger reserve and UNESCO WHS) — second-largest population of one-horned rhinoceros. Also Jaldapara in WB and Pobitora in Assam.

questions.stem: The SNOW LEOPARD is primarily protected in:
questions.explanation: Hemis NP — Leh district, Ladakh. LARGEST National Park in India by area (4,400 sq km). Snow leopard, Asiatic ibex, Tibetan wolf, red fox. Dachigam NP (J&K) is also important (hangul deer).

questions.stem: Which Indian national park is known as the HOME OF THE GREAT INDIAN BUSTARD?
questions.explanation: Desert National Park (Jaisalmer-Barmer, Rajasthan) — stronghold of the Great Indian Bustard (GIB — Ardeotis nigriceps). Critically Endangered; fewer than 150 individuals remain. Also found in Kutch and parts of Karnataka/Maharashtra.
